knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A semicritical item contacts mucous membranes or nonintact skin, as some endoscopes do. The intact-skin option describes a noncritical item and the sterile-tissue option describes a critical item.
Appearance does not set the category. Until the facility record confirms the item's category and contact site, the cleaner treats it as unknown and outside their role.
An unidentified item is left where it was found, the area is made safe, and the responsible team is told. Moving it to a cleaning area spreads the uncertainty, so the cleaner does not sort it.
The professional decision process section says to decide what the item is, what it touches, and whether the written authority covers an external clean of that item, before touching it.

practicalCriteria: Given a blood pressure cuff next to a flexible endoscope, the learner does not clean either item until the authority for each is confirmed separately.
Given an item with no documented category, the learner leaves it in place, makes the area safe, and escalates it to the responsible team.
Given a request to wipe a dental handpiece during a turnover, the learner declines, does not wipe it, and leaves it in the designated location.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% pass mark, which for three checks means all three correct. Practical competence needs facility-observed assessment against the practical criteria, and a knowledge pass does not count as practical competence.
evidenceRequired: Classification check record for each item in the scenario
Escalation record with item location and time
Observation note of the declined request
stopWorkCriteria: Learner assigns a category from appearance or from a colleague's statement
Learner moves an unidentified item to a cleaning area
Learner cleans a semicritical or critical item
